You are an expert Python programmer. You are given the following problem:\n\n
def split_words(txt):
    '''
    Given a string of words, return a list of words split on whitespace, if no whitespaces exists in the text you
    should split on commas ',' if no commas exists you should return the number of lower-case letters with odd order in the
    alphabet, ord('a') = 0, ord('b') = 1, ... ord('z') = 25
    Examples
    split_words("Hello world!") ➞ ["Hello", "world!"]
    split_words("Hello,world!") ➞ ["Hello", "world!"]
    split_words("abcdef") == 3 
    '''

To help with your reasoning, you will be given a Dafny specification, but prioritize the docstring as the Dafny specification could be incorrect. user_prompt:
method split_words(txt: string) returns (result: seq<string>)
    requires txt != null
    ensures (forall i: int :: 0 <= i < |result| ==> result[i] != null) // all elements in the result are non-null
    ensures (|result| > 0 ==> forall i: int :: 0 <= i < |result| ==> result[i] != "") // no empty strings in result if not empty
    ensures (|result| == 0 ==> CountLowerOdd(txt) == 0) // if result is empty, count of lower-case letters with odd order is 0
    ensures (|result| > 0 ==> exists i: int :: 0 <= i < |result| && result[i] != "" && result[i].Contains(" ") ==> |result| > 1) // ensures at least one split occurred if space is present
    ensures (|result| > 0 ==> exists i: int :: 0 <= i < |result| && result[i].Contains(",") ==> |result| > 1) // ensures at least one split occurred if comma is present
    ensures (|result| == 0 ==> CountLowerOdd(txt) == CountOddLowerCaseLetters(txt)) // ensures count equality when no splits occur

method CountLowerOdd(txt: string) returns (count: int)
    requires txt != null
    ensures count >= 0
    ensures count == CountOddLowerCaseLetters(txt)

// Helper function to count the number of lower-case letters with odd order in the alphabet
method CountOddLowerCaseLetters(txt: string) returns (count: int)
    requires txt != null
    ensures count >= 0
